notes: CRITICAL CONTEXT: Both test sources were already processed through /reduce in prior sessions, meaning most content was already in the vault. The with-skill runs correctly detected this prior processing (checking 25-34 existing notes) and adjusted their extraction strategy accordingly. This makes the skip-rate and total-count assertions misleading for with-skill runs.

The 'skip rate below 15%' assertion is non-discriminating in the wrong direction — it penalizes the skill for CORRECTLY detecting prior processing, while baselines that ignore prior state trivially pass by re-extracting everything.

Title-quality assertion ('claims not topics') consistently fails for WITHOUT-skill runs and consistently passes for WITH-skill runs — this is a genuinely discriminating assertion that captures a real quality difference.

The skill adds ~270s average execution time (+78%) and ~21,600 tokens (+32%), largely spent on orientation (reading existing notes, running semantic searches, verifying duplicates). This is expected overhead for vault-aware extraction vs. naive first-pass extraction.

Qualitative differences are more significant than pass rates suggest: with-skill runs produced dangling-link discovery, calibration checks, enrichment tasks, and observations — none of which baseline runs attempted.
